newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court sentences 73 to death, 72 at large.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court sentences 73 to death, 72 at large.

text.p: An Algerian court has passed 73 death sentences in the past month, most on people on the run, the official Algerian news agency said on Tuesday.
The figures from just one courtroom in an Algerian town illustrate the North African country's continuing conflict with Moslem fundamentalists.

APS said in Mostaganem, 260 km (160 miles) southwest of Algiers, the court is trying 150 cases, of which 99 are "linked to criminal acts and sabotage". Algeria uses the term "criminal acts" to describe actions by armed Islamist rebels.
Since the session opened last month, the court has passed 73 death sentences -- 72 of them in absentia -- and sentenced 17 people to life imprisonment, the agency said.
Another 90 people have been given jail terms of 10 to 20 years, while 229 people among a total of 722 accused in the 150 cases were acquitted.
The court session, due to end on November 16, has 26 cases left, 13 of them "linked to criminality and acts of sabotage".
Algeria has been enmeshed in conflict between security forces and Moslem fundamentalists since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by the Islamist Salvation Front.
More than 50,000 people are estimated to have been killed, while sabotage estimated at more than $2 billion has been blamed by the authorities on Moslem rebels.
